scope: Only first selection phase page_table load and resident slot_stamp/slot_ref stores use existing relaxed/device/global atomic_ref<int32_t>. Algorithm, barriers, launch dimensions, queues and pool formats unchanged.
phase_review: Initial group barrier orders epoch reads and tid0 local shared initialization before selection/atomic increments. Temporary global atomic_ref objects end at each statement.

Queries processed in different work-items can access the same block at different selected-ID positions; CAS does not order concurrent ordinary reads, and identical stores are still races. Atomic load/stores remove these three mixed/duplicate access cases.
Selection-ending group barrier orders atomic global accesses before ordinary clock-sweep reads; relaxed device scope suffices for marker/identical-value operations within one work-group.
Legal n_slots>=RT means sweep j=(hand+tid)%n_slots is unique per work-item. Existing block_scan and cut/end-of-iteration barriers order candidate checks and subsequent plain slot updates.

CAS success makes miss_block unique; stamp protects selected/taken slots; legal inverse initial mapping and unique miss slots make placement accesses disjoint. Same in-order queue orders resolve and pool copy kernels.
preconditions: valid ascending IDs within each query, valid inverse map, enough slot/miss capacity, legal integer/epoch lifetime
no overlapping resolves/appends on independent queues using the same map
host USM accesses occur only before submission or after checked completion
